designNotes: The offer is read from the LIVE campaigns row body under the command own prepared transaction, never from a stored private baseline. replayCampaignSourceContracts throws no-private-payload when a stream holds no prior private row, which is the state of every campaign before its first acceptance, so a stored-baseline read would deadlock exactly the case row 3 pins.

sourceRecordBody is JSON.stringify(parsedPayload.body) -- a re-serialization of the parsed stored body, not a byte slice of the payload column. V8 preserves parse-order keys so it round-trips identically in practice, and the baseline digest is computed over the string actually stored, so the envelope stays self-consistent either way. Row 3 pins the round-trip equality against the seeded body.

Fail-closed is UNIFORM: a journal exposing no appendPreparedWithExtension (every in-memory journal) refuses with source-read-unavailable rather than falling back to the caller contract object. That is what changed the three pre-existing AcceptContract rows in campaignCommandPipelineArtifactUse.test.ts. Production always uses SQLiteEventJournal (src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts:130), so no production path lost capability.

The artifact-use consult still runs BEFORE the durable read and still keys on the caller-named contractId -- that is the id being requested, and the durability read then verifies it. The ordering is pinned by the pre-existing sealed-branch row, which still returns invalidated-artifact.

validateCampaignIntent is called INSIDE prepare with the server-derived compact contract substituted, so the faction-standing gate judges the employer the source stored rather than the one the caller typed. This is the shared-validator coupling the admission brief named (CampaignMatchHostIntent.ts:126).

Duplicate-command handling still happens at append time inside appendInTransaction -- i.e. AFTER the offer read. The task text places the duplicate lookup BEFORE the offer read, but that sentence sits in the 6.2b paragraph, and the writer exposes no synchronous receipt read a prepare callback could use. Today it is harmless because 6.2a does not consume the offer from the source record, so a retry still finds it and lands on the append duplicate check. It becomes load-bearing the moment 6.2b writes the reduced market back, and 6.2b owns it.

toolFindings.finding: better-sqlite3 SqliteError does not reliably satisfy instanceof Error under jest
toolFindings.detail: Deterministically reproducible: `npx jest src/lib/campaign src/lib/events/journal` (both parallel and --runInBand) made expect(...).rejects.toThrow(/msg/) report "Received function did not throw" for a promise that demonstrably rejected with that exact SqliteError, and toBeInstanceOf(Error) reported "Expected constructor: Error / Received constructor: SqliteError". The same suite run alone, or together with only src/lib/campaign, passed. Both matchers are built on an instanceof Error check, and the native module prototype chain reaches a different realm Error depending on which suites shared the module registry.
toolFindings.impact: Any assertion on a thrown better-sqlite3 error via .rejects.toThrow / toThrow / toBeInstanceOf(Error) is file-ordering dependent: it can pass in isolation and fail in a wider run, or vice versa.
toolFindings.workaroundUsed: assert err.name === "SqliteError" plus String(err) containing the message -- realm-independent. Verified stable standalone, wide-parallel, and --runInBand.

whyThreeNotTwo.twoLevelAttemptMeasured: The instructed P1a (prepared routing + market read + refusal kind + 409 + artifact-use repoint + refusal rows) measures 4 files / 679 insertions / 49 deletions = 728 changed lines. Over the cap, so the pre-authorized further split was taken.
whyThreeNotTwo.boundaryChosen: Production wiring (prefix 1) separated from the refusal-row suite (prefix 2). The natural alternative -- refusal kind + rows first, prepared routing second -- is not available: the rows cannot be red or green without the routing that produces the refusals.
whyThreeNotTwo.residualOverage: Prefix 1 is 461 insertions / 49 deletions = 510 changed lines: within the cap counting insertions only, 2% over counting insertions + deletions. Reported rather than trimmed.
whyThreeNotTwo.whyNoPartitionDoesBetter: The new suite scaffolding (temp DB, SQLiteService lifecycle, campaigns-row seeder, IContract fixture) is ~150 indivisible lines and must land with at least one row, so wiring (461) + any first row (~172) = ~633 for any prefix holding both. Splitting lower would require either (a) exporting the module-private readCampaignSourceMarket so it could be unit-tested alone -- which changes the final tree and breaks the byte-identity requirement -- or (b) inventing a throwaway plain-append fallback in prefix 1 that prefix 2 deletes. Neither was taken without a decision; both are available if the coordinator prefers a strict <= 500 on the insertions+deletions reading.
